features.name: AI decision matrix
features.description: A framework created to reframe the conversation around AI implementation by focusing on core business functions and transactions with data and people, rather than AI capabilities and hype. Available for download on Red Hawk Technologies website.

features.name: Business-first AI approach
features.description: A strategic approach that recommends starting with business challenges and expensive workflows rather than AI capabilities. Focuses on identifying operational costs, regulatory compliance failures, and transaction-heavy processes before considering AI solutions.
caveats: Requires involvement of business leads in strategic planning
Depends on understanding regulatory and operational context

features.name: Opportunity to cash workflow
features.description: A business framework describing the end-to-end process from identifying a sales opportunity through to revenue recognition. Includes hand-offs from marketing qualified leads to sales intake and deal processing.
caveats: Different companies structure this differently based on offerings

features.name: AI as personal assistant
features.description: Using AI tools for research, analysis, and information organization beyond coding. Applications include portfolio analysis, property comparison, and asking clarifying questions during decision-making processes.
caveats: Requires human review and verification
Requires guidance on what questions to ask

features.name: Agentic workflow optimization
features.description: Using agentic workflows to optimize business process inefficiencies identified through operational analysis of opportunity to cash flows.

features.name: AI notebook as research assistant
features.description: Using notebook tools like Notebook LM to capture transcripts, meetings, and conversations from lead to cash processes and then query AI agents to identify problems and opportunities.
caveats: Requires manual input of interview data and conversations

features.name: AI tool selection guidance for non-technical users
features.description: Recommendation to choose any major AI tool like Chat GPT or Perplexity based on comfort level rather than getting stuck in analysis paralysis, with the principle that starting is more important than choosing the perfect tool.
caveats: Business leaders may need expert guidance on nuances between models
Starting means being willing to change direction

features.name: Data privacy validation for AI tool selection
features.description: Before adopting an AI tool for business use, validate the tool's privacy policy and terms to ensure it does not train on the data you feed it, and create a business-specific account rather than a personal account.
caveats: Privacy policies must be reviewed before use

features.name: AI governance and policy framework
features.description: Implementing structured AI governance with a support group that defines policies for adopted tools, distributes those policies across the organization, and tests employee knowledge before tool onboarding.
caveats: Requires organizational commitment to implement
Must include pre-onboarding training and testing
Scaling challenges when engineering teams grow
Requires enforcement mechanisms

features.name: AI cost monitoring and token limits
features.description: Tokenization costs at scale can become expensive. Organizations need to implement cost controls to prevent unexpected expenses from unmonitored AI usage, which can reach thousands of dollars when left unchecked.
caveats: Cost implications vary by scale and usage patterns

features.name: AI agents with guardrails and boundary setting
features.description: Agents work best when given specific boundaries and instructions to focus output on desired goals. Without guardrails, agents can produce unexpected and potentially problematic results. Engineers use multiple agents with different instruction sets for specific tasks.
caveats: Guardrails can appear to create separate agent instances but are really instruction variations
Setting proper boundaries requires iterative refinement

features.name: Problem-first approach to AI implementation
features.description: Organizations should identify the specific business problem they want to solve before selecting or implementing any AI tool. Starting with problems rather than tools prevents wasted investment and reduces creation of new problems.
caveats: Requires organizational discipline to resist playing with tools
Applies across business sizes

features.name: Data quality prerequisites for AI agents
features.description: Before implementing agents, organizations must have clean, accessible data. Data scattered across multiple locations or stored informally on notepads cannot support effective agent operations.
caveats: Data accessibility and centralization are prerequisites
Data cleanliness is often overlooked

features.name: Fractional CIO model for AI governance
features.description: Smaller mid-market and SMB organizations leverage fractional CIOs for tech stack evaluation and AI policy establishment. These part-time experts are now expected to include AI expertise in their consulting engagements and are becoming essential for smaller organizations.
caveats: Not all organizations need full-time AI oversight roles
Value depends on organization size and complexity

features.name: Multiple AI agents for parallel tasks
features.description: Engineers running five to seven agents at any given point in time to expedite work. Distinction made between actual parallel processes versus multiple instruction sets for single-threaded tasks.
caveats: Many setups with multiple agents are actually single-threaded processes with separate instruction sets, not true parallelization
Agents require guardrails and boundaries to produce acceptable output

features.name: AI-driven quality assurance and testing
features.description: Using AI to create and run automated tests to reduce labor and improve quality throughput. Part of client conversations around adopting AI for business benefit.
caveats: Requires careful adoption and client education
Must deliver tangible improvements in quality and throughput to justify adoption

features.name: Value-based pricing model adoption
features.description: Professional service organizations moving from labor-based to value-based pricing strategies to leverage AI efficiency gains. Consultants helping PSOs modify go-to-market and pricing strategy.
caveats: Requires retooling sales processes and contracts
Organizations must be ready for dramatic business model shifts
Not all markets or customers may accept value-based pricing

features.name: Agentic workflows for CVE remediation
features.description: An AI-powered platform that monitors bill of materials, identifies CVEs, and handles CVE remediation through agentic workflows, automating the process up to pull request generation with engineer notification.
caveats: Human-in-the-loop quality assurance still required

features.name: Automated technical documentation generation
features.description: AI-powered generation of technical documentation for software applications with every commit, reducing manual documentation effort from 80-100 engineering hours to 10 minutes.
caveats: Documentation quality should be reviewed and guided
Can be over-done if not managed carefully

features.name: AI documentation for AI agent maintenance
features.description: Documentation generated by AI can be consumed by AI agents to help maintain software applications, enabling AI-driven application maintenance.
